Upgrades: every contract or node update is submitted, approved and waits a public timelock before it takes effect. Nodes that are too old stop instead of splitting the chain.

Contract update: check out the plan's commit, run cd contracts && forge build, and compare keccak256 of the runtime code with the plan's code hash (cast keccak $(cast code <new code address> --rpc-url https://rpc.psyrob.com)). The node copies the code only if the hash still matches when the timelock ends.

Node update: download the release, run sha256sum SHA256SUMS.txt and compare with the plan; then sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt checks every file. From the activation block, nodes older than the required version stop and say so.

p2p: no handshake with … retrying in … s: the public node could not be reached or refused your address. A refusal (a ban after a node misbehaves) lasts one hour; the node retries by itself, waiting longer each time, up to 5 minutes. Leave it running, and report it if it lasts more than an hour.

Anyone holding 0.5 % of the locked PSY can propose. A proposal passes if yes beats no, yes reaches half the recent turnout, and yes reaches the floor (5 % of locked PSY, 10 % for Treasury, parameter, fund and removal proposals) or enough people voted yes (50, or 100). Then 48 hours of timelock. A token vote that decides an attestation challenge always needs the higher floor (10 % or 100 yes voters). Where 100 yes voters are needed, only voters with at least 100 PSY in their ballot count. A ballot counts the PSY that was locked both when the proposal was made and at the ballot, so PSY locked later adds nothing. A parameter moves at most to double or half its value, once per 30 days.
